{{Short description|Theorem}}
In [[mathematics]] and [[statistics]], '''Skorokhod's representation theorem''' is a result that shows that a [[Weak convergence of measures|weakly convergent]] [[sequence]] of [[probability measure]]s whose limit measure is sufficiently well-behaved can be represented as the distribution/law of a [[pointwise convergence|pointwise convergent]] sequence of [[random variable]]s defined on a common [[probability space]]. It is named for the Ukrainian [[mathematician]] [[Anatoliy Skorokhod|A. V. Skorokhod]].

==Statement==

Let <math>(\mu_n)_{n \in \mathbb{N}}</math> be a sequence of probability measures on a [[metric space]] <math>S</math> such that <math>\mu_n</math> [[convergence in distribution|converges weakly]] to some probability measure <math>\mu_\infty</math> on <math>S</math> as <math>n \to \infty</math>.  Suppose also that the [[support (measure theory)|support]] of <math>\mu_\infty</math> is [[separable space|separable]]. Then there exist <math>S</math>-valued random variables <math>X_n</math> defined on a common probability space <math>(\Omega,\mathcal{F},\mathbf{P})</math> such that the law of <math>X_n</math> is <math>\mu_n</math> for all <math>n</math> (including <math>n=\infty</math>) and such that <math>(X_n)_{n \in \mathbb{N}}</math> converges to <math>X_\infty</math>, <math>\mathbf{P}</math>-almost surely.
